timeline.event: Kyle Theus begins tenancy at 505 S. San Pedro Street Unit 221. One-year lease signed. Only tenancy agreement. No prior eviction notices in approximately nine years.

Notice to Pay Rent or Quit (CARES Act) posted on door by Martha Acosta. Amount demanded $528.00 for period January 1–December 31, 2025. Posting only — no personal service. Internal annotation shows outstanding balance $2,384 — inconsistent with $528 demanded.

Kyle asks Martha Acosta — with Ashley Ross as witness — whether paying full outstanding balance would result in dismissal. Martha confirms yes. Ashley Ross witnesses this exchange. No mention of possession as separate goal.
Complaint prepared by Kimball Tirey & St. John LLP.
Martha Acosta verification on UD-100 complaint is dated one year before complaint filed — potential defect.
Notice of Belief of Abandonment issued by SROHC, signed by Ashley Ross. Sets lease termination date February 11, 2026. Filed day before UD complaint — mutually incompatible legal positions.
UD complaint filed by Gateways Apartment LP — the day after the Abandonment Notice. Limited civil case, amount under $10,000. Plaintiff checked tenancy NOT subject to Tenant Protection Act.
Notice of Unlawful Detainer served on Kyle Theus and all occupants.
Landlord claims personal service occurred this date. Kyle's Answer disputes this.
Kyle files UD-105 Answer — Specific Denials. Fee waiver granted same day. Also constitutes response to Abandonment Notice — one day before February 11 termination date.
Plaintiff requests trial setting. Non-jury trial scheduled for March 13, 2026 at 8:30 AM, Department 91. Electronic service to plaintiff's attorney confirmed.
Plaintiff files Request for Entry of Default against unnamed occupants only — not Kyle Theus who had filed an Answer. Default entered against unnamed occupants.
Kyle contacts Ashley Ross by phone. Confirms payment agreement still operative. Ashley confirms yes. Active logistical coordination begins. Call log documents 5-minute outgoing call at 2:27 PM.

Non-jury trial held at Department 91. Kyle not present — in Tulare assisting grandmother with water damage repairs and cancer-related medical situation. Plaintiff appears. Judge enters judgment for plaintiff.
Judgment entered: Past rent $528.00 plus holdover damages $1,924.72 for total $2,452.72. Possession granted. Lease cancelled and forfeited.

Kyle's brother Keenan arrives at 505 S. San Pedro. Delivers $2,667.00 in money orders to Ashley Ross. First delivery short — Ashley declines partial. Brother returns with corrected full amount. Ashley accepts, issues physical receipt. Transaction complete before 5:00 PM. Exceeds judgment by $214.28.

Ashley calls Kyle. In sequence: (1) states she already informed Martha Acosta of payment; (2) confirms receipt of money orders; (3) asks past-tense whether Kyle was aware of court date. Tells Kyle not to cash money orders — not sure what will happen once things clear up.
Ashley contacts Kyle. States they cannot accept payment. Moving forward with judgment. Institutional reversal communicated.

Writ of possession issued and filed by plaintiff. Application for writ filed same day. Three missed incoming calls from landlord (Debbie) at 4:23 PM, 4:29 PM, and 4:48 PM — landlord called Kyle three times the day writ was issued.

Kyle contacts Ashley. Ashley arranges three-way call with Martha Acosta. Martha refuses to speak in Ashley's presence. Calls Kyle separately from blocked number. States: 'We want judgment. We want possession. We don't want the money; we want possession.' Does not disclose writ issued two days earlier. Kyle makes 10+ outgoing call attempts to reach management throughout day.

Ashley sends email from rtcdevco@gmail.com with subject line 'Re: No Payment Received' — simultaneously transmitting photographs of money orders. Documented contradiction. Highest-value evidentiary item.
Email from Gateways Apartments states money orders being sent back by certified mail and 'You are more than welcome to reach out to the court to file a dismissal.'
Ashley confirms at 2:52 PM: 'Yes, that is the address I have. I will let you know once we send them out.' Money orders NOT sent. Kyle confirms no sheriff's notice posted on door yet.
Ashley emails: 'I have received all of your emails and have forwarded them to Martha and John. Please move forward as you feel necessary.'
Kyle sends URGENT email: 'It has now been six days since I was informed that the money orders were being returned via certified mail.' Documents $2,667.00 figure and delay for court filing.

Money orders still not returned — 34 days since landlord first promised to send by certified mail. 38 days since accepted. Kyle remains in Tulare. Side-by-side notice photograph comparison uploaded showing $528 notice vs $2,384 internal balance vs $2,462.72 judgment.
